ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 32 de 26 de febrero de 1927 (General Corporations Law); Ley No. 4 de 1984 (resident agent regime); Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 and amendments (Panama AML/CFT Law); Ley No. 70 de 25 de marzo de 2019 and Decreto Ejecutivo No. 57 de 7 de mayo de 2021 (final beneficial owner registry); regulations and guidelines issued by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) and the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) implementing beneficial owner declaration obligations through the E-Tax 2.0 platform

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport/identity authority or notary public in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized source-of-funds declaration and current bank reference letter for each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank and notary public in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (bank letter notarized and apostilled, notarized declaration notarized)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney authorizing the Panamanian resident agent and counsel to execute the incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of any corporate shareholder or corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry of the jurisdiction of incorporation of the shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Final Beneficial Owner sworn declaration (Declaración Jurada de Beneficiario Final) to be filed in E-Tax 2.0
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of Panama; prepared by resident agent and UBO

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory CDD/KYC before incorporation: all directors, shareholders, UBOs and authorized signatories must be screened against OFAC SDN, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, EU and UK consolidated sanctions, Interpol notices, Panama's national PEP lists, and adverse media/sources-of-wealth databases; enhanced due diligence is mandatory for PEPs, family members and close associates under Law 23 de 2015 and UAF guidelines; all screening results must be documented in the AML/CFT file maintained by the resident agent.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Portal de Servicios Electrónicos / Aviso de Denominación de Sociedad Anónima (https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name may be in any language using the Latin alphabet, but if Spanish words are used they must follow Spanish orthography; foreign names that could create confusion must be accompanied by a Spanish translation or transliteration recorded in the public deed; the corporate name must include or be followed by 'Sociedad Anónima' or the abbreviation 'S.A.'; names that cannot be clearly transliterated into Latin characters are rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations are valid for thirty (30) calendar days and are not automatically renewable; an unused reservation must be re-submitted as a new application. Upon rejection, the applicant may file a new online solicitud de denominación; if the rejection is considered erroneous, the applicant may file a written reconsideration petition (recurso de reconsideración) with the Director General del Registro Público within five (5) business days under Ley 38 de 2001, and if denied, may pursue a contentious-administrative action before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso Administrativo de la Corte Suprema de Justicia.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office using the resident agent's physical Panamanian address is permissible at formation and for non-operational holding/trading structures in the interactive AI pet robot line; however, if the company imports physical inventory, employs staff in Panama, or maintains a warehouse or retail presence, the DGI and other authorities may require a real operational office with physical files and management presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for the pre-operational shell and agent-only phase: estimated under 5% annual probability of unannounced inspection by Registro Público or DGI; risk rises to an estimated 10–20% annual probability if physical inventory, employees or commercial premises are established in Panama without corresponding substance documentation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 32 of 26 February 1927, the Panama General Corporation Law (Sociedades Anónimas), as amended by Law 11 of 1989, Law 2 of 2012 and related trust and commercial reforms; principally Articles 1-20 (formation and registered agent), 30-42 (share capital and subscription), and 50-60 (directors and officers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección General del Registro Público, Registro Mercantil, Departamento de Personas Jurídicas
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation) to be registered in the Mercantile Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a Panama Sociedad Anónima. Subscribers may pay share consideration in cash, property, or services under terms set by the board. No escrow account or capital deposit proof is required by Law 32 of 1927.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Articles of Incorporation and by-laws are ratified; RESOLVED, that the share subscriptions to the initial authorized shares are accepted and the shares allotted to subscribers; RESOLVED, that the registered office in the Republic of Panama is adopted and the resident agent retained; RESOLVED, that the persons designated in the deed are appointed initial directors and officers, with the corporate records to be kept at the registered office; RESOLVED, that the officers may open bank accounts and execute ancillary filings; RESOLVED, that all acts done to incorporate the Company are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Departamento de Registro de Personas Jurídicas, name reservation counter or official online service window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a written name reservation request selecting one primary and two alternate S.A. names. The applicant subscriber or resident agent must be identified. Pay the name reservation fee and obtain the Name Reservation Certificate before proceeding to the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form signed by the subscriber or resident agent
Copy of passport or national ID of each subscriber
Notarized power of attorney and agent appointment letter if the resident agent acts as representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is disallowed due to conflict or similarity, submit a new ranked list through the same window within five working days or file a written reconsideration petition with the Registro Público; the name certificate fee is not forfeited if an alternative name is selected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Notarial Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Notary Public in the Republic of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Cause the S.A. articles of incorporation to be drafted in Spanish, including corporate name, purpose, registered office address, authorized capital, perpetual duration, registered agent clause, and first directors. The subscribers or their lawful attorneys must appear before the notary, declare the consideration received for the issued shares, and sign the deed; the notary assigns the public instrument number and attests the document.
required_dossiers: Approved Name Reservation Certificate
Draft Escritura Pública de Constitución and by-laws
Passport or national ID of each subscriber and initial director
Original power of attorney if a legal representative signs on behalf of a subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary observes a material defect in the corporate object, name, capital, or agent clause, correct the draft and hold a new attestation; corrections are added to the same instrument and acknowledged before the same notary before registry filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Present Deed and Pay Registry Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Registro Mercantil, Official Collection Office for Registry Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The resident agent or notary presents the notarial deed, the name certificate, and the corporate registration dossier at the Registro Mercantil. The Registry computes filing fees based on authorized capital, notarial copy pages, and the corporate folio. After payment, obtain the stamped received copy and official payment receipt to be attached to the registration file.
required_dossiers: Original notarial deed with notarial stamps
Name Reservation Certificate
Official fee payment receipt
Power of attorney of the presenting resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the document is returned for formal defects, the Registry issues a written observation; the presenter has ten business days to resubmit a corrected deed or rectification note. No second full base fee is charged unless the correction increases authorized capital.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Deed and Obtain Certificate of Juridical Person
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Registro de Personas Jurídicas / Registro Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Registry examiner review, the deed is entered into the Mercantile Register and the Sociedad Anónima becomes a separate juridical person. The resident agent requests an authenticated copy of the registered deed and a Certificado de Persona Jurídica confirming the corporate existence and representation powers.
required_dossiers: Stamped and received copy of the public deed
Registry folio or file number assigned upon presentation
Certificate of no outstanding registry fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry files a vista or query, the deficiency must be cured within ten business days by submitting an explanatory brief and corrected sheet. In case of delayed registration, apply for a provisional certificate and present an administrative appeal to the Director of the Public Registry under the Law 32 review procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt First Board Resolution and Initialize Statutory Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered office of the Company in Panama through the resident agent; notary public may certify signatures if requested by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board of directors meeting, either physically or by unanimous written consent. The first board must ratify the incorporation, accept share subscriptions, adopt the registered office, appoint officers, and approve the bank account opening resolutions. Record the first board resolution in the corporate minute book and issue share certificates with a corresponding share register.
required_dossiers: First board resolution signed by all initial directors
Share subscription agreements and share certificates
Acceptance-of-office statements from the appointed officers
Corporate minute book, share register, and corporate seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or public authority questions officer appointments, cure by delivering a certified extract of the first board resolution and the officers' acceptance forms. If the written resolution contains an omission, obtain a unanimous written consent rectification signed by all directors with notarial authentication if so requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with Tax Administration and Municipal Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Impuestos, Ministry of Economy and Finance, and the Municipality of the registered office (Aviso de Operación window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation documents with the DGI to obtain the Tax Identification Number (RUC), register the legal representative, and submit the initial taxpayer information return. In parallel, file the municipal Aviso de Operación with the local municipality for the industrial or commercial activity. These actions activate the company for fiscal and operational purposes.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Persona Jurídica
Certified copy of the registered public deed
Identification documents of the legal representative and directors
Proof of registered office address, lease deed, or title
RUC registration form executed by the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI or the municipality notes discrepancies between the deed and the application, correct the relevant form through the official portal and present the certified corrected extract. Municipal fines are generally waived if the correction is made before the first annual operating-tax filing deadline.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias de Panamá (MICI), Dirección Nacional de Empresas y Licencias, together with the Municipal Patent Office of the registered domicile
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación and Municipal Commercial-Industrial Business License (Patente Municipal Comercial-Industrial); no separate sectoral concession is required for non-financial robotic toy assembly

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE), Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I – Environmental Registration / Environmental Impact Statement; a full EIA Study is not required for low-impact light assembly of interactive robotic toys using imported non-hazardous components and no significant process emissions
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Panama national air and water quality standards; wastewater discharged to municipal sewer must meet applicable pH, BOD, COD, TSS, VOC, and suspended-solids thresholds. Soldering fluxes, adhesives, paints, lithium battery waste, and electronic scrap must be handled under MiAMBIENTE hazardous waste regulations and Basel Convention transboundary rules. Maintain an environmental monitoring log, quarterly self-audit records, and storage manifests for all special waste streams.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety License from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá after inspection of exit routes, extinguishers, and evacuation plans; municipal architecture clearance verifying structural load and seismic safety of the assembly area; Ministry of Labor (MITRADEL) and Ministry of Health occupational workplace clearance covering noise exposure, machine guarding, electrical safety, and first-aid facilities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; online taxpayer portal: Sede Electrónica DGI – https://dgi.mef.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Panama Sociedad Anónima, the resident agent files incorporation articles with the Registro Público and obtains the corporate 'ficha', then applies to the DGI for the Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC). Required submissions include notarized articles of incorporation, identification of directors and the resident agent, proof of registered address, and a sworn registration affidavit. The DGI issues the RUC and, when applicable, the ITBMS tax registration certificate. A Panamanian digital signature (Firma Digital) is required for Sede Electrónica access. The municipal Aviso de Operación is also required before commencing commercial activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide US-style check-the-box elections; classification follows civil-law form and the S.A. is a distinct legal entity taxed only on Panamanian-source income under the territorial system. Taxpayers may apply for the simplified small-taxpayer ITBMS regime (gross receipts not exceeding B/.36,000 annually), voluntary advanced pricing arrangements with the DGI, and certain import-processing or free-zone customs regimes; no general tax-consolidation or hybrid-mismatch election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) – Panamanian VAT-equivalent
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold; every person or entity undertaking taxable transfers of movable goods or rendering taxable services in Panama must register. A distinct simplified small-taxpayer regime applies to annual gross receipts not exceeding B/.36,000 (Panamanian balboas, at par with USD).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates phased electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) through DGI-authorized systems. Invoices must be digitally signed using the taxpayer's Firma Digital and transmitted near-real-time to the DGI's Sede Electrónica or a certified service provider; each invoice receives a unique fiscal code and must display a valid QR/electronic seal. Non-compliant invoices are not admissible for ITBMS input credits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods qualify for 0% ITBMS when the goods are physically removed from Panamanian territory under a valid customs export declaration. Exported services, i.e. services performed for a non-resident and utilized or commercially exploited entirely outside Panama, are also zero-rated. The exporter must retain complete proof of export and source documentation demonstrating actual foreign destination or offshore benefit.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI and the National Customs Authority jointly audit export zero-rating claims using risk matrices. Where the zero rate is improperly applied, the DGI retroactively assesses unpaid ITBMS with monthly interest and a 25% surcharge, plus fines up to 100% of the omitted tax under the Tax Code. False or fabricated export documentation may trigger customs smuggling penalties, criminal prosecution, forfeiture of refunds, and exclusion from public procurement.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the banking, trust, and payments regulator; Banco Nacional de Panamá (BNP) acts as the State's fiscal agent and clearing-house operator, but Panama has no issuing central bank, no monetary authority, and no statutory foreign-exchange control body.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a legally dollarized jurisdiction: the United States dollar is constitutional legal tender, and the Panamanian balboa (PAB) circulates only as subsidiary coinage at a fixed 1:1 parity with USD. Current-account and capital-account transactions are fully convertible with no exchange controls, no registration gates, and no prior approval for capital entries or exits. Profit remittance and dividend repatriation are unrestricted at the market-operational level; the only practical hurdles are Panamanian territorial-tax withholdings on domestically sourced distributed profits and the corporate governance documentation required by banks (UBO declaration under Law 70 of 2019, resident agent certificate, and good-standing certificate).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panamanian law imposes no mandatory surrender, compulsory conversion, or statutory repatriation timeline for export receipts. An exporting S.A. may retain proceeds in USD or any foreign currency in onshore or offshore accounts without SBP notification; banks only document wire transfers under the AML/CFT framework (FATF Recommendation 16 remittance rules) and do not apply exchange-control limits.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low-to-Moderate. Panama's Law 75 of 2021 (fintech sandbox) does not establish a full electronic-money-institution license, and offshore digital EMIs (electronic money institutions) are not permitted to run balance-holding payment accounts inside Panama without SBP authorization. Foreign EMIs (e.g., Mercury, Payoneer, relay-type platforms) frequently screen out PAN-domiciled non-resident manufacturing S.As. When available, an EMI may serve only as a thin collection sub-account, with automatic daily sweeping via SWIFT MT103 to the primary licensed Panamanian bank account; legal constraint is the absence of EMI passporting and the SBP's requirement that Panama-situs payment activities be performed by licensed banks or licensed payment service providers.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, a physical in-branch KYC interview of at least one director or the designated authorized signatory is required by most Panama banks; fully remote opening is not standard for a foreign-owned non-resident S.A. A notarized and apostilled board resolution appointing a Panamanian attorney-in-fact or resident agent as banking representative can substitute for the director's physical appearance, subject to enhanced due diligence and a local notarized witness signature. BAC Credomatic and Global Bank offer some digital onboarding only for resident individuals, not for this corporate profile. Budgeted assumption: one authorized principal must personally visit Panama City for account opening and secondary signatory setup.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity: nominee shareholders, possible bearer-share legacy, or undisclosed ultimate beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing from the Registro Público de Panamá; certified share ledger and certified copy of the Law 70 of 2019 UBO register filing; resident agent's compliance certificate identifying all final natural persons; signed beneficial ownership disclosure form (actual and intended).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate ownership and absence of an existing banking relationship in Panama.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passports and professional references of shareholders, directors, and authorized signatories; bank references from the home-jurisdiction bank; proof of economic substance for PA_CORP (office lease, local payroll records or operations plan, water/utility invoices); notarized and apostilled board resolutions for account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Manufacturer/importer business profile: expected global card settlement flows through Stripe and credit-card acquirers, with robotics hardware (ISIC 3240 / NAICS 339930) trade in Asia and Latin America.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan with sales-and-volume forecast; audited or draft financial statements; ISIC/NAICS classification letter; signed purchase orders, pro-forma invoices, supplier contracts, and one-to-two years of merchant-account statements when available; inventory and logistics documentation proving genuine commercial activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce credit-card refunds, chargebacks, and third-party payment settlement flows triggering irregular-transaction monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant acquiring agreement and gateway reconciliation reports; documented refund/chargeback policy; ERP payment reconciliation procedures; bank reference confirming operational backing; customer-dispute log showing low historical chargeback ratios.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and geographic concentration: component suppliers or consumer markets in high-risk or restricted jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country-of-origin certificates, customs entry filings, bills of lading, and commercial invoices; OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening policy, procedure, and software logs; confirmation that PA_CORP has no dealings in sanctioned jurisdictions and maintains a third-party screening program administered by the resident agent or compliance officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire routing uses SWIFT MT103 with Field 70 remittance information strictly identified as APORTE DE CAPITAL - PA_CORP or SHAREHOLDER LOAN - PA_CORP; banks classify the credit by concept and require the supporting board resolution, apostilled formation documents, UBO register receipt, and source-of-funds declaration. Panama requires no SBP prior approval, no balance-of-payments registration, and no special-purpose escrow for capital inflows; once received, the treasury department tags the funds in the ERP as equity or intra-group debt and mirrors the entry in the S.A.'s books. For card-generated treasury inflows, Stripe does not natively support Panama-domiciled sellers; the PA_CORP must route e-commerce collections through a supported foreign merchant-of-record or local payment facilitator, with USD sweeps from the acquiring settlement account to the Panamanian treasury account via SWIFT/Fedwire ACH on a daily T+1 schedule.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Routine supplier settlements are executed via SWIFT MT103/MT202 through SBP-regulated banks to Asian and European component suppliers, with any required FX spot conversion. High-value purchase orders for robotic-animal components and speech-synthesizer modules are settled using commercial documentary letters of credit issued under UCP 600 by Banistmo or Banco General, advised through correspondents in the supplier country, with reimbursement governed by URR 725. Domestic USD payments within Panama clear through the local clearing-house ACH and check-clearing rails operated under the Banco Nacional de Panamá. Credit-card and Stripe settlement flows land in the operational account as USD credit via Fedwire/CHIPS, SWIFT, or local ACH; refunds and chargeback reserves are held at the merchant acquiring level to protect the primary treasury account from debits.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/foreign-exchange spot and outright forward contracts transacted with licensed Panamanian banks (no regulatory approval required; valuation at market rates)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on regional Latin American currencies (COP, MXN, BRL) desk-executed through international correspondent banks of the local institution
Cross-currency swaps (fixed/floating and fixed/fixed) for intra-group shareholder loans or material trade payables denominated in EUR, CNY, or JPY
Vanilla over-the-counter and exchange-traded foreign-currency options (calls and puts) on major convertible currencies for risk-limited hedging of projected trade flows

Natural hedging via multi-currency deposit and settlement accounts (USD, EUR, CNY) opened with Towerbank or Global Bank to structurally offset non-USD trade payables without entering derivative contracts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual franchise tax (Impuesto Único Anual) for Sociedad Anónima
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 July of each calendar year, irrespective of accounting year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a 10% surcharge plus statutory interest on the unpaid fee, denial of tax good-standing certificates; persistent non-payment for two or more tax periods permits the Registro Público de Panamá to initiate administrative strike-off of the corporation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Registro de Beneficiarios Finales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual declaration due on or before 31 July; changes in shareholding must be reported within 15 working days of any direct or indirect transfer of shares
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines from USD 250 to USD 5,000 for late or incomplete filings; temporary suspension of the company's right to obtain certificates and legal standing sanctions may apply in the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax declaration (Declaración Anual de Renta, Form 230)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; for calendar-year companies, due by 31 March. No filing requirement if the company has no Panamanian-source taxable income.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of 5% to 15% of the tax due, monthly interest of 1.5% on arrears, potential tax lien against corporate assets, and criminal tax liability for grossly fraudulent declarations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Panama Law does not require a general independent audit for an ordinary Sociedad Anónima. Audited financial statements are mandatory for regulated financial entities, securities market issuers, and companies separately required by the DGI or by their own bylaws; DGI may also request audited statements where annual gross revenue exceeds USD 2,000,000 or in sector-specific determinations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Panamanian statutory accounting follows NIF (Normas de Información Financiera), which adopt IFRS as issued by the IASB; SMEs may apply NIF para Pymes. For tax purposes, financial statements must comply with these standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The resident agent must submit an annual UBO confirmation with the DGI Beneficial Owner Registry by 31 July. In addition, any share transfer or change in ultimate ownership must be notified to the registry within 15 working days, with supporting documents (transfer deed, updated share register, legal entity ownership chart) kept at the registered office. Failure to maintain an accurate UBO file or to report movements may invalidate transfers for company-law purposes and trigger monetary penalties.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 1,200 per year depending on service provider, including registered office, resident agent, and compliance support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - USD 6,000 per year where an audit is required or requested; most non-regulated small SAs incur zero audit expenditure

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% top marginal CIT rate on taxable income exceeding USD 1.5 million, applied through a graduated bracket structure (15% on the first USD 11,000; 25% on the band from USD 11,001 to USD 50,000; 27.5% on the band from USD 50,001 to USD 1,500,000; 25% above USD 1,500,000).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to ISIC 3240 robotic toy assembly; the principal effective relief is territoriality, which excludes foreign-source revenue from the Panamanian tax base. Export sales of AI pet robots delivered and invoiced outside Panama are foreign-source income and thus exempt. Standard deductions for manufacturing inputs, depreciation of automated assembly machinery, and research-and-development expenses are available under DGI criteria. No special economic-zone or reforestation credit applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 105 (Declaración Anual de Impuesto sobre la Renta) filed through the Panamanian Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) electronic platform known as E-Tax (Sistema Informático de la DGI).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year taxpayer the annual return and settlement of the balance due are due no later than March 31 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate legal name, Panamanian RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes), fiscal year-end, domicile, resident agent (agente residente), and registered shareholders/beneficial owners registry identifiers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the S.A.'s Panamanian RUC; disclose the resident agent and the final beneficial ownership identifiers required by Law 21 of 2017/Law 70 of 2019; a foreign sole shareholder is permissible with no additional local tax classification filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 — Ingresos Gravables de Fuente Panameña
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue derived from activities performed, goods delivered, or services rendered within Panamanian territory, including domestic e-commerce sales and local retail of robotic units.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Panama-source e-commerce and credit-card receipts; sales to overseas consumers with delivery outside Panama are not included in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 — Ingresos de Fuente Extranjera (Exentos por Territorialidad)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenues sourced outside Panama under the territoriality principle, including exports of assembled AI pet robots destined to foreign customers and payments received abroad for foreign intellectual-property exploitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a reconciliation schedule showing foreign shipping documentation, customs exit certificates, and Stripe settlement records segmented by country; foreign-source gross receipts must be excluded from the taxable base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ordinary and necessary expenses attributable to Panama-source income: raw materials, components, direct labor, depreciation of robotic assembly lines, engineering overhead, freight for domestic distribution, and R&D outlays within Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses attributable to exempt foreign-source income are non-deductible and must be segregated; payments to non-residents that fail to apply the correct withholding are disqualified and trigger a gross-up adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed taxable net income after deduction of authorized costs and the pro-rata apportionment of mixed expenses; the graduated brackets are then applied to this figure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the bracket thresholds in Balboas (USD equivalent): first USD 11,000 at 15%, the next band to USD 50,000 at 25%, the band to USD 1.5 million at 27.5%, and the excess at 25%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 — Impuesto Determinado, Créditos por Pagos Directos y Saldo a Pagar
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual tax payable reduced by the monthly advance payments (pagos directos) credited; any balance due must be remitted with the return; overpayments are carried forward as a credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the 12 monthly Formulario 101 prepayments or the two semiannual installments (15 August and 15 November) under the modality elected; a non-resident group's Panamanian S.A. is a taxpayer in its own name and cannot consolidate with the foreign parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Anexo TP — Operaciones con Partes Relacionadas
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory disclosure of related-party transactions with intercompany purchases, financing, royalty payments, and management fees exceeding the statutory threshold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the TP annex if aggregate related-party transactions exceed USD 1,000,000 or if free-zone export price arrangements are used; state the arm's-length method applied and prepare corresponding Local File documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic 10% surcharge on the total tax payable, monthly interest of 1% computed on the unpaid balance, and an administrative fine of up to USD 5,000 per return. Non-filing or incomplete filing permits DGI best-judgment assessments with an additional 20% recrimination surcharge, and persistent default exposes directors to criminal proceedings for fiscal fraud.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 101 (Declaración Mensual de Pagos Directos) filed through the same DGI E-Tax portal for the prepayment methodology of corporate income tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on the 15th day of each month following the month to which the advance corresponds; if the 15th falls on a non-business day, payment shifts to the next business day. Under Modality B, two semiannual installments of 50% each are due on 15 August and 15 November.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1 — Ingresos Brutos Estimados del Mes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimated gross Panama-source revenues expected for the month, used to compute the advance base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Estimate strictly from Panama-sourced turnover; do not anticipate exempt foreign export revenue unless the funds have already cleared through the Panamanian banking system.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory deduction coefficient applicable to the commercial and industrial category of the taxpayer; the manufacturing category for ISIC 3240 is subject to the standard coefficient determination of the DGI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Request a prior confirmation letter from DGI if the taxpayer intends to apply a coefficient outside the prescribed table; misuse creates an illegal deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance computed under Modality A (1/12 of prior-year tax) or Modality B (semiannual installment), whichever has been elected in the DGI registry.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If prior-year tax was zero, file a nominal zero advance but support the calculation; a zero balance on the annual return does not excuse non-filing of monthly prepayments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 4 — Acumulado de Pagos a Acreditar
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Running cumulative deposit of advances available for credit on the annual Formulario 105.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain bank payment receipts per month; discrepancies between the accumulated credit and DGI's payment record are a common audit trigger for foreign-held companies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Omission of a required monthly advance produces interest at 1% per month, a fine of 25% of the omitted amount, and the automatic loss of the elected prepayment modality, followed by immediate full assessment of the remaining annual tax before the original filing deadline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 106 (Declaración del Impuesto sobre Dividendos / Distribución de Utilidades) filed through the DGI E-Tax portal at the moment profits are distributed.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Event-driven (filed every time the S.A. approves a profit distribution, whether cash, physical asset, or share-based).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within ten calendar days following the date of the general shareholders' meeting resolution declaring the dividend or the actual payment date, whichever occurs first.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross amount of the profit distribution in Balboas/USD, including cash dividends and non-cash distributions at fair market value.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all classes of economic benefit conferred on the foreign shareholder; disguised distributions (excessive management fees, forgiven shareholder loans) must be reclassified on audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cumulative register of earnings already subject to corporate income tax within the S.A.; only distributions covered by this register attract the 10% complementary dividend tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain the taxed-earnings register with audited working papers; distributions in excess of this register are treated as untaxed earnings and attract a 20% withholding rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable at the statutory 10% rate on the gross distribution carved from the taxed-earnings register.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not exempt from this charge by mere territoriality; a treaty reduction applies only where the Panama DTA concerned provides a lower rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 — Convenio de Derechos de Autor / Tratado Invocado
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of any Double Taxation Agreement (DTA) invoked, the Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) reference, and the reduced withholding rate claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the certified TRC issued by the foreign tax administration and the Formulario 106 annex for treaty relief; Panama's DTA network in force includes the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, Spain, Portugal, Luxembourg, Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, Mexico, France, Switzerland, and South Korea.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers the 10% surcharge plus monthly 1% interest; an unreported distribution outside the taxed register is reclassified at the 20% rate with interest and a fine of USD 5,000, and directors who approve the distribution are jointly and severally liable for the uncollected tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% complementary dividend withholding tax on distributions made out of the register of taxed earnings; 20% on distributions made from untaxed earnings or from the untaxed portion of the taxed register.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief the corporate secretary must (1) obtain from the foreign shareholder a certified Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued within the same calendar year, (2) complete the treaty relief annex of Formulario 106 in the E-Tax portal before paying the dividend, (3) submit the TRC, DTA analysis, and beneficial-ownership declaration via the DGI's electronic communication module, and (4) retain the approved relief documentation with the corporate books for at least five years, because the DGI requires the beneficial owner to be the taxpayer as opposed to a conduit entity; a treaty claim made without a TRC or based on a nominee shareholder is rejected and the 10%/20% statutory rates are assessed retroactively.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid by the Panamanian S.A. to a non-resident lender is exempt from Panamanian withholding tax where the loan funds are deployed outside Panama or the credit is extended from a foreign head office without a local permanent establishment; interest on funds used within Panama is Panama-source and subject to a 25% statutory withholding rate, reducible to treaty rates (typically 5% to 10%). Royalties and license fees for the AI speech-synthesizer and robotic patents paid to non-residents for intellectual property used inside Panama are subject to a 25% statutory withholding tax, reducible under DTA provisions to 5% to 10%; royalties paid for exploitation of the software/synthesizer captive in servers located outside Panama are foreign-source and attract zero Panamanian tax. Payments made through Stripe or credit-card processors to a non-resident for services delivered abroad are not subject to withholding absent a Panama PE.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 1,000,000 (B/.1,000,000) in aggregate related-party transactions during a fiscal year, which activates mandatory Local File and Master File preservation in accordance with Executive Decree 165 of 2011 and OECD-aligned DGI Resolution criteria; multinational groups with consolidated revenue equal to or greater than USD 850,000,000 must additionally file Country-by-Country reporting with the DGI.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama Law 254 of 2021 (Economic Substance Regulations) classifies manufacturing of goods — expressly including the assembly of bionic robotic pet units under ISIC 3240 — as a designated relevant activity, so the S.A. must demonstrate compliance through a physical office in Panama, inspection of qualified engineering and production staff in Panama, execution of strategic management meetings in Panama, and operating expenditure proportional to revenue derived from the activity. The economic substance test must be evidenced through payroll records, lease agreements, board minutes, and cost accounting in Panama. Failure of an ESR review exposes the entity to administrative fines from USD 5,000 to USD 50,000, revocation of the fiscal certificate of economic substance, and ultimately strike-off of the registry of companies; treaty benefits and attributions of profits to the Panamanian entity may also be denied in international audits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of Panama-source e-commerce and credit-card sales of AI pet robots collected through Stripe/Payment Card rails; creation of false invoices to shift profit to a foreign shell; claiming territorial exemption on revenue actually delivered to Panama customers; or fraudulent overstatement of the taxed-earnings register to avoid the 10% dividend tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Fiscal Code imposes a 10% late surcharge, monthly interest of 1%, administrative fines up to USD 5,000 per return, and recalculations demanding up to 200% of the evaded tax. The Criminal Code (as integrated into fiscal matters) punishes fiscal fraud with imprisonment of two to ten years depending on the amount, confiscation of assets, and permanent exclusion from state contracting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the S.A. who sign a fraudulent return or direct the evasion lose the protective veil under Panamanian piercing doctrine: civil restitution for the full evaded amount plus interest, court-issued travel bans (veda de salida) during the fiscal investigation, and imprisonment for aggravated cases; the nominee resident agent who assists the scheme is also exposed to disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Failure of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining no physical office in Panama, holding board meetings exclusively abroad, employing zero staff in Panama, retaining bearer shares outside a licensed custodian, or failing to file the annual economic substance declaration while claiming full treaty benefits for dividend repatriation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 254 of 2021 the penalty range is USD 5,000 to USD 50,000 per default, with escalation to suspension of the corporate rights and cancellation of the registry entry if the deficiency is not cured within the statutory notice period; Law 47 of 2013 imposes a fine of up to USD 10,000 for each violation of the bearer-share custody rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors cannot invoke the corporate shield where the S.A. functions as a pure instrument of the foreign parent; personal liability attaches for the unpaid corporate income tax of the manufacturing activity, and directors may be barred from acting as officers or managers in Panama for up to ten years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Integration of Stripe and credit-card payment volumes without a written AML/KYC program, non-registration of the final beneficial owner in the Registro Público as required by Law 70 of 2019, maintenance of anonymous corporate-owned merchant accounts, or acceptance of revenue derived from a predicate tax offense into the corporate bank account.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law 23 of 2015 empowers the Unidad de Análisis Financiero to impose fines of up to USD 1,000,000 per violation, to suspend the account, and to coordinate asset seizures; a criminal money-laundering prosecution can run concurrently with tax evasion and carries imprisonment of five to twelve years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who designate a nominee without record-keeping, who fail to adopt customer due-diligence protocols for merchant sales, or who sign shipments supporting fraudulent invoices face freezing orders, travel bans, disqualification from Panamanian financial industry positions, and criminal liability for money laundering where the funds in the corporate account trace to tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming a treaty-reduced dividend withholding rate for a foreign shareholder lacking Tax Residency Certificate, routing dividends through a conduit entity that does not satisfy beneficial-ownership conditions, or extracting profits as deductible royalties/interest rather than equity distributions to avoid the 10% dividend tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI recharacterizes the payment as a distribution, applies the 20% untaxed-earnings rate, adds the 10% late surcharge and 1% monthly interest, and levies an additional abuse-of-treaty penalty of 50% of the avoided withholding tax; the treaty relief certificate is revoked and a second infraction triggers publication in the official registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who certify the TRC or approve the conduit structure are personally assessed for the uncollected withholding amount and must compensate the corporate treasury; prolonged abuse constitutes fraudulent breach of fiduciary duty under Law 32 of 1927, enabling civil suits by minority shareholders and foreign partners, plus potential criminal prosecution for forgery where the TRC documentation is materially falsified.
